notes.title: Tea Garden Simulator 1.0 Release Notes Sneak Peek
notes.content:
Hello Tea heads!

We just wanted to share a list of the most interesting features and fixes you can expect in the Tea Garden Simulator 1.0 release.

[h3]General [/h3]
We are upgrading the leaf inspector with a real time flow visualization of you flavor compounds forming and dissipating via your processing. This single UI in addition to other existing graphs which are upgraded, will instantly inform the player about which process is forming the compounds and how to improve on them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38855962/692fbd500daeb7fcae2286b7b0a5ed7c8f2c1dc2.png[/img]

A brand new panel to see the available cultivars. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38855962/d0ab8ad3ecb1a351365cfc112213069b0708a639.png[/img]

The processing machines now behave more predictively and under a unified processing model.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38855962/33ecd2f63a3e695fd8114f768aaccdf76d1b62ac.png[/img]

[h3]Bugfixes :[/h3]

Leaf Inspector now remembers last settings of the leaf.
Looped Package Visualization in Store.
Automation line loading bug.
UI upgrade in leaf inspector.
Hovering on flavor compounds indicates their flavor in Flavor profile.
Trimming down machine sliders.
Altitude is now separate on cultivar panel.
Impact of treatment on tea plant more explained and predictable.
UI inconsistency between store and factory.
Out of stock bug in store after removing product.
Bug in plucking after switching plucking methods.
Graphics bug in level layout.
PNG artifact in water level.
Weed removal balancing.
Oxidation now has helper. To point out missing enzymes.
Sales count bug in store.
After medium prune, plant still produce leaves normally.
Shade tree button grey out when shade trees are planted. 
Factory speed now resets on turn end.
Machine timer resets when leaves are dropped on machine.
UI overlap in factory.
0 Kgs are not plucked.
Production in fields are now capped. 
Toolbox bugfix and upgrade
Loading sometime was getting into weird game state, not anymore.
Sales model fix.
Selecting field opens up plucking tab.
Residual 1 sec removed from factory time after machine stops.
Leaf Inspector now remembers last settings of the leaf.

[h3]Steam Features :[/h3]
24 achievements.
Steam Cloud support.

[h3]Beta Invitation for Early Access Backers :[/h3]
Please note that these changes are not live yet. But you can play the beta of the release build by mailing us at beta@syvgames.com. We will send instructions for you.

notes.title: Update 9/22
notes.content:
Hello, teaheads,

We are happy to implement more features in this update.

1. The change of seasons now affects the color palette of the entire level. In addition to that, the fog and cloud cover and rain fx are also added.

2. We are introducing a bunch of BRAND NEW tea processing equipment which can be helpful in preparing more variations of tea.

a) Hand rolling - This manual process is extremely helpful for subtly damaging your tea and processing it again for more flavors. Make sure you keep an eye on the chemical charts for better understanding.

b) Hand Tossing - This is even subtler than hand rolling. This tradition of bruising tea is quite common among oolong producers. This method is for further tweaking your tea flavors.

c) Bruising Machine - This tumbling machine is predominant in oolong factories. They are trying to mimic hand shaking or tossing via a machine. But can it really replace manual bruising? What do you think?

d) Sha Qing Wok - This is the staple equipment for Chinese producers. It's still an irreplaceable part of tea production, especially Puerh. A hard labor-intensive process, but with its benefits.

e) Automated Sha Qing Machine - This is the automated version of sha qing wok. Fast, efficient. But, will it give the same quality as manual sha qing? You have to experiment with it to find out. 

f) Steaming Machine - This is also a very popular option. Especially among Japanese and Indian green tea producers. But you have to tweak your pipeline a bit to accommodate this.

g) Ball Rolling Machine - This is popular among Oolong producers. Especially who like to preserve the volatiles. 

h) Rack Drying Machine - No fuss, efficient and effective. But they give a slightly different result than the traditional roasting machine.

i) Charcoal Roasting - This is quite a specialty tea equipment. We are really unsure about its effectiveness apart from the nuances it brings in flavors. We tried our best to implement it. Let us know the results. 

There are also numerous small improvements and bug fixes apart from these. But we don't want to bore you with that. Go ahead and play with these new toys and let us know what you think.

Cheers

notes.title: Huge Update - Complete rewrite
notes.content:
This is the upgrade that we've been promising for the better part of a year.

The entire game has been completely redone from the ground up. Only the visual materials were reused in this project. The reason behind this is that the game has shifted from being a mid-core simulation game to a hard-core simulation game. Because the prior version and the architecture were unable to support the elaborate and complicated gameplay we were aiming for, we had to abandon them.

However, it took significantly longer than we had anticipated. And here's what came out of it. The game does not even come close to the previous version in terms of quality.

These are some of the most important aspects of what you can expect.

The simulation engine was completely rewritten to simulate over 46 different flavour compounds derived from a total of ten precursor chemicals. (There were just two in the prior edition.)

The development of precursor chemicals is influenced by the time of year. Cultivation stress is being simulated.

Apart from soil and other elements, the land now has an impact on the precursor growth of the tea plant, which was formerly influenced by them.

The presence of amino acids in the chloroplasts was used to simulate the presence of clones/cultivar genes in the cells.

In this version of the simulation model, numerous loops are combined to get a more complex yet consistent output.

The machines have a more objective impact on the simulation and do so through a defined set of settings.

These are only a few of the numerous features of this new version.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38855962/a63efe06024d42b3a6d808672a98d6d1df3d6fd6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38855962/7ae1bd9a93c58d3106625e6e2aa0261bfaa8f348.png[/img]


You are more than welcome to experiment with this new build. Your feedback will only help the sim engine to improve in the future. This build is still in the process of being tested. As a result, there may be bugs. Please let us know about it in our discord group.

Hopefully, this new build will prove to be well worth the wait.

Cheers.

Cultivation stress is being simulated.
Apart from soil and other elements, the land now has an impact on the precursor growth of the tea plant, which was formerly influenced by them.
The presence of amino acids in the chloroplasts was used to simulate the presence of clones/cultivar genes in the cells.
In this version of the simulation model, numerous loops are combined to get a more complex yet consistent output.
The machines have a more objective impact on the simulation and do so through a defined set of settings.
